## 2

I understand why some people feel suspicious of official images, especially when institutions have made mistakes before. But the evidence for a round Earth doesn’t depend on trusting space agencies or a single photograph. Ships disappear hull-first over the horizon, different stars are visible from different latitudes, Earth’s shadow on the Moon during eclipses is round, and people can circumnavigate the planet. Satellites, GPS, long-distance flights, and observations made independently by ordinary astronomers also fit a spherical Earth much better than a flat one. What kind of evidence would you consider convincing?

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors—red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and violet. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more than most other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from across the sky. That is why the sky usually looks blue. At sunset, sunlight has to travel through more atmosphere, which scatters away much of the blue and leaves more red and orange light for us to see.

## 4

雨下了一整夜，细密的水声敲打着窗玻璃，像有人在黑暗中轻轻叩门。街灯被雨幕晕成一团温黄的光，积水映着屋檐和电线，偶尔被驶过的汽车划碎。远处传来模糊的雷声，城市仿佛沉入一场漫长的梦里。屋内只亮着一盏小灯，茶杯边升起淡淡的热气。我靠在窗前，看雨水蜿蜒而下，忽然觉得这样的夜晚虽然寂静，却也温柔得令人安心。
